searches.query: "Jensen v. BMW of North America" 35 Cal.App.4th 112 civil penalty "section 340"
searches.result: Saved (FindLaw mirror). searches.query: "Hypertouch, Inc. v. ValueClick" 192 Cal.App.4th 805

Reaffirms Jensen/Holland for penalties the court may decline to award.

authorities.cite: Granberry v. Islay Investments (1995) 9 Cal.4th 738
authorities.holding: A landlord that in good faith failed to use the deduct-and-retain procedure may recover unpaid rent, repair and cleaning damages by setoff or claim in a later judicial proceeding on proof by a preponderance and of reasonableness; equitable defenses available (pp. 749-750).
authorities.dicta: Fn. 6: no opinion on rights of bad-faith landlords. P. 745: without a timely accounting the right to retain is not perfected and the landlord must return the entire deposit. Characterizes bad-faith damages as a 'penalty'.
authorities.later_history: Scholar cited-by list filtered to 'bad faith' (23 results) read 2026-10-03: no published case resolving fn. 6 or limiting the holding; applied by analogy in 250 L.L.C. v. PhotoPoint (2005). Partly superseded in practice by AB 2801's express bad-faith forfeiture (h)(7), which is consistent with the holding. No citator.

authorities.cite: Granberry v. Islay Investments (Cal. Ct. App. 1993), superseded by grant of review
authorities.holding: (Superseded) approved a subjective bad-faith instruction: retention with belief it was not authorized by statute; honest mistake or negligence is not bad faith.
authorities.later_history: Superseded by the Supreme Court's grant of review; Supreme Court did not review the instruction ruling (9 Cal.4th at p. 743, fn. 4).

authorities.cite: 250 L.L.C. v. PhotoPoint Corp. (USA) (2005) 131 Cal.App.4th 703
authorities.weight: binding on Civ 1950.7; persuasive analogy for 1950.5
authorities.holding: Under Civ 1950.7 a landlord may apply a deposit only to rent accrued by the statutory return date; reading Granberry, a good-faith violator may offset only amounts it properly could have claimed of the deposit.
authorities.later_history: Cited in AB 2801 Senate Judiciary analysis (2024). Modified on denial of rehearing Aug. 29, 2005 without change in judgment. No citator.

authorities.cite: Peviani v. Arbors at California Oaks Property Owner, LLC (2021) 62 Cal.App.5th 874
authorities.holding: Reversed denial of class certification, including a security-deposit class; liability turns on reasonableness of deductions (common), bad faith goes to statutory ('punitive') damages which can be decided separately.
authorities.dicta: Statement of the elements of a 1950.5 wrongful-retention claim.
authorities.later_history: Review denied July 14, 2021 (per Western Center summary; not independently verified). No citator.

authorities.cite: Orozco v. Casimiro (2004) 121 Cal.App.4th Supp. 7
authorities.holding: A residential lease's flat $50 late fee is void under Civ 1671(d) where the landlord neither pleads nor proves that damages were impracticable or extremely difficult to fix.
authorities.later_history: Cited in DRE 2026 tenants guide. Not a deposit bad-faith case. No citator.

authorities.cite: Holland v. Nelson (1970) 5 Cal.App.3d 308
authorities.holding: Discretionary treble damages are not a 'penalty or forfeiture'; CCP 338 (three years) applies.
authorities.later_history: Followed by Menefee (1991) and Jensen (1995); acknowledged in Hypertouch (2011); no disapproval located (Scholar search 2026-10-03). No citator.

authorities.cite: Menefee v. Ostawari (1991) 228 Cal.App.3d 239
authorities.holding: Mandatory treble damages under SF rent ordinance are a penalty subject to CCP 340(1); discretionary multiple damages are not (following Holland).
authorities.later_history: Followed in Jensen (1995); cited in Prudential (1998). No citator.

authorities.cite: Jensen v. BMW of North America, Inc. (1995) 35 Cal.App.4th 112
authorities.holding: Song-Beverly discretionary civil penalty (up to two times actual damages for willful violation) is governed by the four-year period of the underlying action; CCP 340(1) applies only to mandatory penalties (p. 133).
authorities.later_history: Relied on in Hypertouch (2011) and Shamsian v. ARCO (2003). No citator.

authorities.cite: Prudential Home Mortgage Co. v. Superior Court (1998) 66 Cal.App.4th 1236
authorities.holding: Mandatory $300 forfeiture under Civ 2941(d) is a penalty subject to CCP 340(1); discovery rule may apply.
authorities.dicta: Restates 'settled rule' that double or treble damages are penal; disagrees with MacManus.
authorities.later_history: Cited in Low v. Lan (2002). No citator.

authorities.cite: Hypertouch, Inc. v. ValueClick, Inc. (2011) 192 Cal.App.4th 805
authorities.holding: Liquidated damages mandatory once claimed and proven are a penalty under CCP 340 even though the court sets the amount (following TJX Companies (2008) 163 Cal.App.4th 80).
authorities.dicta: Reaffirms Jensen/Holland rationale for discretionary awards.
authorities.later_history: Opinion on rehearing Feb. 10, 2011. No citator.

authorities.cite: Hagey v. Solar Service Experts, LLC (2023) 94 Cal.App.5th 1303
authorities.holding: Monthly billing for electricity already supplied, with no prepayment, is a consumer credit transaction under Rosenthal.
authorities.later_history: Modified Sept. 26, 2023 without change in judgment (Oct. 1 research). Echoed by Assembly Banking staff analysis of SB 546 (June 2026). No citator.

authorities.cite: Davidson v. Seterus, Inc. (2018) 21 Cal.App.5th 283
authorities.holding: 'Credit' means acquiring value without immediate payment on a promise of future payment; Rosenthal's collector definition does not import the FDCPA default-at-acquisition limit.
authorities.later_history: Relied on by Assembly Banking staff (2026). No citator.

authorities.cite: Olson v. La Jolla Neurological Associates (2022) 85 Cal.App.5th 723
authorities.holding: A creditor that exclusively retains an unaffiliated billing company is not itself a Rosenthal debt collector on that record; actual participation and control decide.
authorities.later_history: No citator.

authorities.cite: De Dios v. International Realty & Investments, 641 F.3d 1071 (9th Cir. 2011)
authorities.holding: A residential property manager that obtained the right to collect rent before default is excluded from 'debt collector' by 1692a(6)(F)(iii); default is judged by contract and state law at the time the debt is obtained.
authorities.dicta: Declined to decide whether a servicer meets the primary definition.
authorities.later_history: Applied in Yatooma (C.D. Cal. 2017). No later published Ninth Circuit decision revisiting it located by web searches; Scholar citing search blocked. No citator.

authorities.cite: Reichert v. National Credit Systems, Inc., 531 F.3d 1002 (9th Cir. 2008)
authorities.holding: A collector that added a landlord-supplied fee not authorized by the lease violated 1692f(1); reliance on the landlord's past accuracy and a conclusory procedures affidavit did not establish the bona fide error defense.
authorities.later_history: Not checked beyond the Oct. 1 work. No citator.

authorities.cite: McAdory v. M.N.S. & Associates, LLC, 952 F.3d 1089 (9th Cir. 2020)
authorities.holding: A debt purchaser whose principal purpose is collection is a debt collector even if it outsources contact.
authorities.later_history: Not checked beyond the Oct. 1 work. No citator.

authorities.cite: Henson v. Santander Consumer USA Inc., 582 U.S. 79 (2017)
authorities.holding: A purchaser collecting defaulted debts for its own account is not collecting debts 'owed ... another'; principal-purpose prong left open.
authorities.later_history: Principal-purpose prong addressed by McAdory (9th Cir. 2020).

authorities.cite: Romine v. Diversified Collection Services, Inc., 155 F.3d 1142 (9th Cir. 1998)
authorities.holding: A service provider that contacted debtors, obtained their numbers and relayed collection messages for collectors may be a debt collector that collects 'indirectly'; reversed dismissal.
authorities.later_history: Not checked. No citator.

authorities.cite: Yatooma v. OP Property Management LP, No. 2:17-cv-02645 (C.D. Cal. July 20, 2017), ECF 27
authorities.holding: Owner and manager not FDCPA debt collectors (property management primary function; originated the lease); advance rent later unpaid is not Rosenthal consumer credit.
authorities.later_history: No citator.

authorities.cite: Brooks v. Greystar Real Estate Partners, LLC, No. 3:23-cv-01729-LL-VET, ECF 48 (S.D. Cal. Sept. 26, 2024)
authorities.holding: 1950.5 and UCL claims against the manager sufficiently pleaded (systematic missing documentation, flat cleaning fees, late refunds alleged in bad faith); owner entities indispensable only for relief extinguishing balances they own; UCL four-year period governs class period.
authorities.later_history: Followed by ECF 56 (Aug. 7, 2025); case in putative-class discovery Sept. 2026; Ninth Circuit denied Rule 23(f) petition Dec. 17, 2025.

authorities.cite: Brooks v. Greystar Real Estate Partners, LLC, ECF 56 (S.D. Cal. Aug. 7, 2025)
authorities.holding: Owner SPEs not necessary parties because return of deposits is complete relief available from the manager (citing Granberry, (h)(7), Leaser); struck 'Unauthorized Deduction Class' because 1950.5(b) 'any purpose' allows utility charges.
authorities.later_history: Ninth Circuit denied Rule 23(f) petition Dec. 17, 2025 (ECF 68).

authorities.cite: Leaser v. Prime Ascot, L.P., No. 2:20-cv-02502-DJC-AC, ECF 60 (E.D. Cal. June 12, 2024), 2024 WL 3011226
authorities.holding: A manager that orchestrated alleged excessive-fee and deposit practices may be liable in UCL restitution even if the funds went to owners; absent owners not required parties.
authorities.later_history: GovInfo package shows only a July 19, 2024 stipulation afterwards. No citator.

authorities.cite: Sen. Judiciary Com., Analysis of AB 2801 (2023-2024 Reg. Sess.) as amended Apr. 25, 2024, hearing June 11, 2024
authorities.dicta: (h)(7) requires a good-faith attempt, not strict adherence; good-faith violator may offset (citing PhotoPoint).
authorities.later_history: Final Senate amendments chaptering-only (Assembly floor analysis, Aug. 2024).

authorities.cite: Assem. Floor Analysis, Concurrence in Senate Amendments, AB 2801 as amended Aug. 23, 2024
authorities.dicta: Senate amendments: chaptering amendments to resolve conflicts with SB 611.

authorities.cite: Sen. Com. on Banking & Fin. Institutions, Analysis of SB 908 (2019-2020 Reg. Sess.) as amended Apr. 15, 2020
authorities.dicta: Senate Judiciary staff: licensing aimed at those spending a considerable portion of their business collecting consumer credit debt; incidental collectors excluded.

authorities.cite: Assem. Com. on Banking & Finance, Analysis of SB 908, hearing Aug. 12, 2020
authorities.dicta: DCLA uses Rosenthal definitions; Real Estate Law licensees exempt.

authorities.cite: Assem. Com. on Banking & Finance, Analysis of SB 546 (2025-2026 Reg. Sess.), hearing June 22, 2026
authorities.dicta: Advance rent not RFDCPA credit; postpaid utilities are; billing agents for rent/utility statements implied to be DCLA licensees; sponsor Conservice DCLA-licensed.
authorities.later_history: SB 546 ordered to Assembly inactive file Aug. 17, 2026; not enacted.

authorities.cite: DFPI PRO 05/21 third prefiling draft text (Oct. 24, 2025)
authorities.dicta: Draft 10 CCR 1850.2(a)(1): residential rental debt not consumer debt for DCLA (COVID exception struck); draft 1850.1: 100001(b)(1) exemption limited to listed licensees and employees.
authorities.later_history: DFPI page (2026-10-03) shows no formal notice or adoption.
Enacted 1872; unchanged.
